displayedInputs.question:
There are 5 small blocks visible from the front and 3 visible from the side. How many more blocks are visible from the front than from the side? Calculate: \(5-3=?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

What is the area, in square centimeters, of a parallelogram with a base of 7 centimeters and a height of 4 centimeters?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

What is the area, in square centimeters, of a triangle with a base of 8 centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters?

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

What is the area, in square centimeters, of a trapezoid with an upper base of 2 centimeters, a lower base of 6 centimeters, and a height of 4 centimeters?

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

What happens when you view a simple object from the front, the side, and above?

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

choices.A: The shapes you see may be different
choices.B: The views from all three directions must be the same
choices.C: You can only see the top

displayedInputs.question:
You see 4 blocks from above and 2 layers from the front. If every column is 2 blocks high, how many blocks are there altogether? Calculate: \(4\times 2=?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

How many faces does a rectangular prism have?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

How do the edge lengths of a cube compare?

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

choices.A: They are all the same length
